"""Revenue-surprise credit-extension trap.

Mechanism: a positive revenue surprise is more likely to represent low-quality,
credit-supported sales when receivables outgrow revenue and collection days also
rise versus the comparable period a year earlier.  The interaction distinguishes
aggressive customer financing from benign billing timing or productive onboarding.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _credit_extension_trap(
    revenue_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    receivables_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    dso: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal report-window interaction between credit growth and slower collection.

    Fundamental inputs are point-in-time quarterly step functions.  A change in
    revenue growth marks a newly available report; the 252-bar DSO lag compares
    the latest collection state with an approximately comparable prior-year date.
    """
    rev = revenue_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    rec = receivables_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    surprise = revenue_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    clean_dso = dso.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    fresh = rev.notna() & rev.ne(rev.shift(1))
    prior_year_dso = clean_dso.shift(252)
    dso_change = clean_dso / prior_year_dso.where(prior_year_dso > 0.0) - 1.0

    credit_wedge = rec - rev
    collection_deterioration = dso_change.clip(lower=0.0)
    valid = (
        fresh
        & (surprise > 0.0)
        & (rev > 0.0)
        & credit_wedge.notna()
        & collection_deterioration.notna()
    )

    trap_intensity = (credit_wedge * collection_deterioration).where(valid)
    event_score = rank(trap_intensity).where(valid, 0.5).where(fresh)
    return event_score.ffill(limit=6)


@register_factor
class SurpriseCreditExtensionTrap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "surprise_credit_extension_trap"

The adverse interpretation becomes much more credible when year-over-year DSO also rises, because the additional receivables are not merely a billing-timing effect but are taking longer to collect. This interaction should carry edge because Parent B identifies the credit-supported growth state while Parent A supplies the collection-duration evidence that disambiguates productive ramping from low-quality revenue recognition; high trap scores are expected to precede lower six-bar returns.

"""Deleveraging-validated earnings attention gap.

Mechanism: a muted earnings reaction is informative when the same filing shows
that operating cash is servicing and retiring debt, rather than financing the
business externally. Stable share count makes that financial improvement more
likely to accrue to incumbent equity holders.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_flag(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """First available bar for a point-in-time fundamental update."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    return clean.notna() & (prior.isna() | clean.ne(prior))


def _event_carry(value: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame, carry: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Freeze an event-date quantity for a finite causal holding interval."""
    return value.where(event).ffill(limit=carry - 1)


@register_factor
class DeleveragingValidatedEarningsAttentionGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "deleveraging_validated_earnings_attention_gap"
    name = "Deleveraging-Validated Earnings Attention Gap"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Fresh EPS-surprise reaction deficits, retained for six bars only when "
        "the contemporaneous filing shows cash debt service, debt retirement, "
        "and relatively stable ownership."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsSurprise",
        "sharesGrowth",
        "marketCap",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "totalDebt",
        "netDebtIssuance",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        share_growth = data["sharesGrowth"].reindex_like(close)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close)
        operating_cash = data["operatingCashFlow"].reindex_like(close)
        total_debt = data["totalDebt"].reindex_like(close)
        net_debt_issuance = data["netDebtIssuance"].reindex_like(close)

        surprise_update = _update_flag(surprise)
        cash_update = _update_flag(operating_cash)
        funding_update = _update_flag(net_debt_issuance)
        report_event = surprise_update & (cash_update | funding_update)

        ret = close.pct_change()
        idio_response = ret.sub(ret.median(axis=1), axis=0)

        debt_base = total_debt.where(total_debt > 0.0)
        equity_base = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)
        cash_service = operating_cash / debt_base
        debt_retirement = -net_debt_issuance / equity_base

        # Cross-sectional ranks use only the information public on this bar.
        surprise_signal = rank(surprise) - 0.5
        response_signal = rank(idio_response) - 0.5
        funding_strength = 0.5 * rank(cash_service) + 0.5 * rank(debt_retirement)
        ownership_strength = rank(-share_growth)

        event_surprise = _event_carry(surprise_signal, report_event, 6)
        event_response = _event_carry(response_signal, report_event, 6)
        event_funding = _event_carry(funding_strength, report_event, 6)
        event_ownership = _event_carry(ownership_strength, report_event, 6)

        deficit = event_surprise - event_response
        aligned_underreaction = (event_surprise * deficit) > 0.0
        active = (
            event_surprise.notna()
            & event_response.notna()
            & event_funding.notna()
            & event_ownership.notna()
            & aligned_underreaction
        )

        score = (event_surprise * deficit.abs() * event_funding * event_ownership).where(active)
        return rank(score).where(active, 0.5).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Deleveraging-Validated Earnings Attention Gap
programs.trading_idea: An earnings surprise whose idiosyncratic price response is too muted should drift only when the accompanying cash-flow disclosure establishes that the per-share earnings update is financially durable: operating cash covers debt and the firm is retiring rather than issuing debt. Stable or declining share count further makes the benefit belong to incumbent shareholders rather than being diluted away. The interaction has edge because a reaction deficit alone can reflect low-quality or externally financed earnings, while deleveraging alone is slow-moving; a muted reaction to a cash-funded, ownership-preserving report identifies detailed balance-sheet information that the headline-price response has not yet incorporated.
programs.description: On fresh, jointly observed earnings and cash-flow updates, the factor ranks the signed EPS-surprise reaction deficit and weights it by cash debt-service capacity, debt retirement, and ownership stability. Scores are frozen for six bars after the report and inactive names receive a neutral value.

"""Cash profitability residual: cash returns can reveal earnings quality missed by accrual ROIC.

Mechanism: firms with operating-cash-flow returns on invested capital above their
reported ROIC have more cash-realized profitability than conventional accounting
quality screens imply.  This persistent discrepancy should be incorporated only
gradually after sector-relative comparison of quarterly financial statements.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class CashReturnAccrualRoicResidual(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_return_accrual_roic_residual"
    name = "Cash Return versus Accrual ROIC"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral rank of operating-cash-flow return on invested capital "
        "minus the cross-sectional rank of reported ROIC."
    )
    window_length = 1
    inputs = ["close", "sector", "operatingCashFlow", "investedCapital", "roic"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        capital = data["investedCapital"].where(data["investedCapital"] > 0.0)
        cash_return = (data["operatingCashFlow"] / capital).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        accrual_roic = data["roic"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        discrepancy = rank(cash_return) - rank(accrual_roic)
        sector_relative = indneutralize(discrepancy, data["sector"])
        return rank(sector_relative).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cash Return versus Accrual ROIC
programs.trading_idea: The child retains the parent's core insight that internally generated cash is more informative than headline accounting delivery, but removes sparse report-event gates, financing branches, and short-lived muted-price-response conditions. Firms whose operating-cash return on invested capital exceeds their reported accrual ROIC have earnings that are more cash-realized than the market's standard profitability screens imply; this should predict positive six-bar returns as investors gradually incorporate the higher-quality profitability. The mechanism is falsified if the cash-return-minus-ROIC residual has no positive forward-return spread after sector neutralization and conditioning on reported ROIC itself. The edge can persist because common quality and benchmark processes emphasize reported earnings and ROIC, whereas cash-flow realization is quarterly, less salient, and costly to arbitrage through shorting low-quality firms.
programs.description: Ranks each firm's operating-cash-flow return on invested capital relative to its reported ROIC, then sector-neutralizes the discrepancy. High values identify firms with unusually strong cash realization relative to accrual profitability.

"""Expensive firms with worsening cash collection face near-term earnings-quality repricing.

A fresh decline in cash realization is most adverse when receivables growth is
accelerating and the stock is expensive on free-cash-flow yield.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_change(value: pd.DataFrame, limit: float, halflife: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal quarterly-update impulse, decayed after its public availability."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    updated = clean.notna() & prior.notna() & clean.ne(prior)
    change = (clean - prior).clip(lower=-limit, upper=limit)
    impulse = np.tanh(change).where(updated, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    return impulse.ewm(halflife=halflife, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()


@register_factor
class ExpensiveCashCollectionDeterioration(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "expensive_cash_collection_deterioration"
    name = "Expensive Cash-Collection Deterioration"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "High values identify expensive firms with a newly worsening cash-to-income "
        "relationship and accelerating receivables growth, signalling an earnings-" 
        "quality reassessment risk."
    )
    window_length = 12
    inputs = ["close", "incomeQuality", "receivablesGrowth", "freeCashFlowYield"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        quality = data["incomeQuality"].reindex_like(close)
        receivables_growth = data["receivablesGrowth"].reindex_like(close)
        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].reindex_like(close)

        # A negative income-quality update means less operating cash per unit of income.
        quality_deterioration = (-_fresh_change(quality, 2.0, 3.0)).clip(lower=0.0)
        collection_acceleration = _fresh_change(receivables_growth, 1.0, 3.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        expensive = (-fcf_yield).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        score = quality_deterioration * collection_acceleration * expensive

        return score.rank(axis=1, pct=True).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Expensive Cash-Collection Deterioration
programs.trading_idea: A fresh deterioration in cash realization combined with accelerating receivables growth is evidence that reported earnings are becoming less collectible rather than merely temporarily volatile. The child concentrates this accounting-quality warning in expensive firms, where valuation relies most on continued conversion of reported profits into cash and a reassessment can occur within the following week. The edge should persist because investors and event-driven traders often initially focus on headline earnings, while distinguishing a working-capital-driven quality deterioration requires slower balance-sheet parsing; the hypothesis is falsified if high-score names do not underperform after fresh cash-conversion deterioration, particularly in the expensive valuation subset.

"""Credit-financed buyback narrative fracture after fresh revenue surprises."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_relative_state(value: pd.DataFrame, floor: float = 0.01) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally retain newly disclosed changes while allowing report information to decay."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    changed = clean.notna() & prior.notna() & clean.ne(prior)
    update = ((clean - prior) / prior.abs().clip(lower=floor)).where(changed, 0.0)
    update = update.clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)
    return update.ewm(halflife=6, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()


def _fresh_level_state(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry a newly reported level briefly without repeatedly scoring stale filings."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    changed = clean.notna() & prior.notna() & clean.ne(prior)
    update = clean.where(changed, 0.0).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)
    return update.ewm(halflife=6, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()


@register_factor
class ReceivableBuybackNarrativeFracture(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "receivable_buyback_narrative_fracture"
    name = "Receivable-Buyback Narrative Fracture"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Fresh positive revenue surprises are scored most negatively when excess "
        "receivables growth coincides with buyback-supported EPS acceleration and "
        "weakening operating-cash realization."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "revenueGrowth",
        "receivablesGrowth",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsGrowth",
        "operatingMargin",
        "revenuePerShare",
        "sharesGrowth",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        revenue_growth = data["revenueGrowth"].reindex_like(template).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        receivables_growth = data["receivablesGrowth"].reindex_like(template).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(template).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_state = _fresh_relative_state(data["epsGrowth"].reindex_like(template))
        margin_state = _fresh_relative_state(data["operatingMargin"].reindex_like(template))
        revenue_ps_state = _fresh_relative_state(data["revenuePerShare"].reindex_like(template))
        buyback_state = _fresh_level_state(data["sharesGrowth"].reindex_like(template))
        ocf_state = _fresh_relative_state(data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(template))
        quality_state = _fresh_relative_state(data["incomeQuality"].reindex_like(template))

        fresh_report = revenue_growth.notna() & revenue_growth.shift(1).notna() & revenue_growth.ne(revenue_growth.shift(1))
        valid = fresh_report & surprise.gt(0.0) & receivables_growth.notna()

        credit_wedge = (receivables_growth - revenue_growth).where(valid)
        credit_pressure = (rank(credit_wedge).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)

        eps_acceleration = rank(eps_state).fillna(0.5) - 0.5
        operating_delivery = 0.5 * (rank(margin_state).fillna(0.5) - 0.5) + 0.5 * (rank(revenue_ps_state).fillna(0.5) - 0.5)
        unsupported_eps = (eps_acceleration - operating_delivery).clip(lower=0.0)
        buyback_support = (rank(-buyback_state).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)

        cash_fragility = (
            0.65 * (rank(-ocf_state).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)
            + 0.35 * (rank(-quality_state).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)
        )

        fracture = credit_pressure * buyback_support * unsupported_eps * (1.0 + 2.0 * cash_fragility)
        event_score = rank(fracture.where(valid)).where(valid, 0.5)
        return event_score.ffill(limit=6).reindex_like(template).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Receivable-Buyback Narrative Fracture
programs.trading_idea: A positive revenue surprise funded by an unusually large receivables build is more concerning when management simultaneously relies on buybacks to produce EPS acceleration while operating-cash conversion deteriorates. The receivable wedge alone can reflect legitimate customer onboarding, and buybacks alone can be a credible capital-return policy; their conjunction identifies a more specific state in which credit-financed reported growth and denominator management jointly preserve an earnings narrative despite weakening cash realization. This should precede negative six-bar returns as investors reassess whether the beat represents durable demand or sales pulled forward through customer financing and financial engineering.
programs.description: On fresh positive-revenue-surprise reports, the signal ranks the interaction of excess receivables growth, buyback-supported EPS acceleration versus operating delivery, and deteriorating cash conversion. High scores denote the most fragile credit-and-buyback-supported earnings narratives.

"""Collection-integrity deleveraging attention drift.

Mechanism: a positive earnings surprise that receives too little immediate price
response is more likely to drift when operating cash supports debt retirement and
sales quality is corroborated by disciplined receivables and collection duration.
This excludes superficially strong reports whose revenue may be credit-supported.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _fresh_update(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag the first bar on which a point-in-time field changes."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    return clean.notna() & (prior.isna() | clean.ne(prior))

def _carry_event(value: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame, bars: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally retain an event-date observation over a short holding interval."""
    return value.where(event).ffill(limit=bars - 1)

@register_factor
class CollectionIntegrityDeleveragingAttentionDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'collection_integrity_deleveraging_attention_drif'
    name = 'Collection-Integrity Deleveraging Attention Drift'
    category = 'other'
    description = 'Ranks muted positive EPS-surprise reactions only when contemporaneous cash deleveraging, stable ownership, and disciplined receivables and collection duration jointly validate the report.'
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ['close', 'epsSurprise', 'operatingCashFlow', 'totalDebt', 'netDebtIssuance', 'marketCap', 'sharesGrowth', 'revenueGrowth', 'receivablesGrowth', 'daysSalesOutstanding']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        surprise = data['epsSurprise'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        operating_cash = data['operatingCashFlow'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        total_debt = data['totalDebt'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        debt_issuance = data['netDebtIssuance'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_cap = data['marketCap'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        share_growth = data['sharesGrowth'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_growth = data['revenueGrowth'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        receivables_growth = data['receivablesGrowth'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        dso = data['daysSalesOutstanding'].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        report_event = _fresh_update(surprise)
        idio_return = close.pct_change().sub(close.pct_change().median(axis=1), axis=0)
        debt_base = total_debt.where(total_debt > 0.0)
        equity_base = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)
        cash_service = operating_cash / debt_base
        debt_retirement = -debt_issuance / equity_base
        prior_dso = dso.where(_fresh_update(dso)).ffill().shift(1)
        dso_change = dso / prior_dso.where(prior_dso > 0.0) - 1.0
        credit_wedge = receivables_growth - revenue_growth
        surprise_rank = rank(surprise) - 0.5
        response_rank = rank(idio_return) - 0.5
        funding_strength = 0.5 * rank(cash_service) + 0.5 * rank(debt_retirement)
        ownership_strength = rank(-share_growth)
        collection_strength = 0.5 * rank(-credit_wedge) + 0.5 * rank(-dso_change)
        event_surprise = _carry_event(surprise_rank, report_event, 6)
        event_response = _carry_event(response_rank, report_event, 6)
        event_funding = _carry_event(funding_strength, report_event, 6)
        event_ownership = _carry_event(ownership_strength, report_event, 6)
        event_collection = _carry_event(collection_strength, report_event, 6)
        deficit = event_surprise - event_response
        aligned = (event_surprise > 0.0) & (deficit > 0.0)
        active = aligned & event_funding.notna() & event_ownership.notna() & event_collection.notna()
        raw_score = (event_surprise * deficit * event_funding * event_ownership * event_collection).where(active)
        return rank(raw_score).where(active, 0.5).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Collection-Integrity Deleveraging Attention Drift
programs.trading_idea: A muted positive earnings surprise should drift when cash-funded deleveraging makes the earnings update durable, but only if receivables and collection duration do not deteriorate alongside the report. This conditions Parent B's attention-gap mechanism on the inverse of Parent A's credit-extension state: the market is more likely to underreact to a financially improving report when sales are also being collected normally. Neither parent alone separates a quietly underreacted durable earnings update from an apparently cash-rich report whose revenue quality is weakening.
programs.description: On fresh positive EPS-surprise dates, the factor ranks the positive reaction deficit after multiplying it by deleveraging, stable-share-count, and collection-integrity scores. Collection integrity rewards receivables growth below revenue growth and non-increasing DSO versus the prior disclosed state, with the signal retained for six bars.

"""Prompt forensic repricing after a failed filing-day acceptance.

Mechanism: a sales beat accompanied by worsening collection duration and income
quality is fragile.  If an initially positive reaction closes well below its
intraday high, informed holders may be distributing into filing liquidity;
the resulting short-lived adverse-selection signal predicts a prompt reversal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Keep sparse point-in-time fields numeric without fabricating reports."""
    return df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class ForensicDSOCloseRejectionShort(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "forensic_dso_close_rejection_short"
    name = "Forensic DSO Close-Rejection Short"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Shorts fresh positive sales-surprise filings with worsening DSO and "
        "income quality when a positive filing-day rally closes far below its "
        "intraday high; the event remains active only briefly."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "daysSalesOutstanding",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        close = _finite(template).reindex_like(template)
        high = _finite(data["high"].reindex_like(template))
        low = _finite(data["low"].reindex_like(template))
        surprise = _finite(data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(template))
        dso = _finite(data["daysSalesOutstanding"].reindex_like(template))
        income_quality = _finite(data["incomeQuality"].reindex_like(template))

        # Quarterly fields are forward-filled.  A changed surprise identifies a
        # newly available filing without looking ahead or shifting fundamentals.
        prior_surprise = surprise.shift(1)
        fresh_filing = (
            surprise.notna()
            & prior_surprise.notna()
            & surprise.ne(prior_surprise)
        )

        # Credit-funded delivery appears as slower cash collection and weaker
        # conversion of accounting earnings into operating cash.
        dso_worsening = dso - dso.shift(1)
        quality_worsening = income_quality.shift(1) - income_quality
        credit_score = (rank(dso_worsening).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)
        cash_score = (rank(quality_worsening).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        prior_vol = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        reaction_z = ret / prior_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        positive_reaction = (rank(reaction_z).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)

        # A large upper wick after a positive reaction is a failed acceptance:
        # the market traded higher on the headline but could not retain that level.
        day_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        upper_wick = ((high - close) / day_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        rejection = (rank(upper_wick).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)

        valid = (
            fresh_filing
            & surprise.gt(0.0)
            & dso_worsening.notna()
            & quality_worsening.notna()
            & reaction_z.notna()
            & upper_wick.notna()
        )

        impulse = (
            credit_score * cash_score * positive_reaction * rejection
        ).where(valid, 0.0)

        # A short deterministic disclosure-auction clock avoids rewarding a
        # stale quarterly wedge whose correction belongs to a longer horizon.
        prompt_state = impulse.rolling(3, min_periods=1).max()
        return rank(prompt_state).reindex_like(template).fillna(0.5)

def _collection_strain(
    receivables_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    dso: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    rec = receivables_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    rev = revenue_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    clean_dso = dso.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    prior_dso = clean_dso.shift(63).where(lambda x: x > 0.0)
    dso_worsening = (clean_dso / prior_dso - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)

    return rank(credit_wedge) + rank(dso_worsening)

        close = data["close"]

        cash_return = (data["operatingCashFlow"] / capital).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        accrual_roic = data["roic"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_residual = rank(cash_return) - rank(accrual_roic)

        # Quarterly point-in-time working-capital values are forward-filled.

The hypothesis is falsified if the negative forward-return spread is not concentrated among high-residual firms with working-capital liquidation, or if the same residual has an equally negative spread when working capital is stable or expanding. """Working-capital harvest pressure following quarterly financial-statement updates.

Mechanism: cash flow that exceeds reported ROIC can be transitory when it is
created by releasing working capital rather than by durable operating
profitability.  A recent contraction in working capital identifies this source
of cash; investors can initially reward the cash result before reassessing its
sustainability over the next several trading days.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _harvest_pressure(
    operating_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame,
    invested_capital: pd.DataFrame,
    roic: pd.DataFrame,
    working_capital: pd.DataFrame,
    total_assets: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal, decayed score for cash flow sourced by working-capital release.

    Balance-sheet fields are point-in-time step functions.  Their one-bar
    difference is therefore nonzero only when a newly available report changes
    the reported balance-sheet state; the EWM carries that disclosure's
    information forward without using future observations.
    """
    capital = invested_capital.where(invested_capital > 0.0)
    cash_return = (operating_cash_flow / capital).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    reported_roic = roic.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    cash_residual = rank(cash_return) - rank(reported_roic)
    positive_cash_residual = cash_residual.clip(lower=0.0)

    prior_assets = total_assets.shift(1).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    working_capital_change = working_capital - working_capital.shift(1)
    contraction = (-working_capital_change / prior_assets).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )

    # Relative ranks make the accounting scale robust; only above-median
    # contractions activate the temporary-cash-flow interpretation.
    contraction_strength = (rank(contraction) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)
    disclosure_pressure = positive_cash_residual * contraction_strength

    # A three-day half-life makes a report-date diagnosis actionable at the
    # configured six-bar forecast offset while remaining entirely trailing.
    return disclosure_pressure.fillna(0.0).ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False).mean()


@register_factor
class WorkingCapitalHarvestDisclosureDecay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "working_capital_harvest_disclosure_decay"
    name = "Working-Capital Harvest Disclosure Pressure"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral rank of recently disclosed working-capital contraction "
        "interacted with positive operating-cash-return versus ROIC residuals. "
        "High values identify cash profitability likely sourced by temporary "
        "balance-sheet release."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "investedCapital",
        "roic",
        "workingCapital",
        "totalAssets",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        pressure = _harvest_pressure(
            data["operatingCashFlow"],
            data["investedCapital"],
            data["roic"],
            data["workingCapital"],
            data["totalAssets"],
        )
        sector_relative = indneutralize(pressure, data["sector"])
        return rank(sector_relative).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

"""Delayed audit of quietly accepted credit-funded revenue beats.

Mechanism: a positive sales surprise is less credible when receivables expand
faster than revenue while operating cash flow fails to keep pace.  When the
headline receives a positive but low-turnover price response, detailed cash
reconciliation is likely to arrive with delay; the causal decay carries this
initially accepted narrative-fracture state into the next week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _clean(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove non-finite accounting observations without inventing values."""
    return df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class SilentAcceptanceCreditCashAuditUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "silent_acceptance_credit_cash_audit_unwind"
    name = "Silent Acceptance Credit-Cash Audit Unwind"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Shorts newly reported positive revenue surprises whose receivable and "
        "cash-flow delivery disagree, but only after a positive low-turnover "
        "price acceptance; the event score decays causally across the audit lag."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "revenueGrowth",
        "receivablesGrowth",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        close = _clean(template).reindex_like(template)
        volume = _clean(data["volume"].reindex_like(template))
        revenue_growth = _clean(data["revenueGrowth"].reindex_like(template))
        receivables_growth = _clean(data["receivablesGrowth"].reindex_like(template))
        ocf_growth = _clean(data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(template))
        surprise = _clean(data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(template))

        prior_revenue_growth = revenue_growth.shift(1)
        fresh_report = (
            revenue_growth.notna()
            & prior_revenue_growth.notna()
            & revenue_growth.ne(prior_revenue_growth)
        )

        # Relative accounting wedges are ranked over the full available universe,
        # avoiding unstable ranks among the small set of same-day reporters.
        credit_wedge = (receivables_growth - revenue_growth).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        cash_wedge = (revenue_growth - ocf_growth).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        credit_pressure = (rank(credit_wedge).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)
        cash_pressure = (rank(cash_wedge).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change()
        prior_volatility = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        reaction_z = ret / prior_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        accepted = (rank(reaction_z).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        quiet_attention = (
            rank(-np.log(relative_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))).fillna(0.5) - 0.5
        ).clip(lower=0.0)

        valid = (
            fresh_report
            & surprise.gt(0.0)
            & receivables_growth.notna()
            & ocf_growth.notna()
            & reaction_z.notna()
            & relative_volume.notna()
        )

        # Zero is an explicit non-event: EWM then implements a deterministic,
        # trailing audit clock rather than repeatedly rewarding stale filings.
        event_impulse = (
            credit_pressure * cash_pressure * accepted * quiet_attention
        ).where(valid, 0.0)
        audit_state = event_impulse.ewm(halflife=4, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

        return rank(audit_state).reindex_like(template).fillna(0.5)

"""Cash-validated trade-credit demand response.

Mechanism: following a positive revenue surprise, receivables growing faster than
sales can reflect commercially productive trade-credit expansion rather than
aggressive revenue recognition when operating cash flow is also improving.
The market initially discounts the sales signal for collection risk, then
updates as cash validation makes demand capture more credible.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _validated_credit_demand(
    revenue_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    receivables_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_cash_flow_growth: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build a causal report-event score from point-in-time fundamentals."""
    rev_growth = revenue_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    rec_growth = receivables_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    surprise = revenue_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cash_growth = operating_cash_flow_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    fresh = surprise.notna() & surprise.ne(surprise.shift(1))
    credit_wedge = rec_growth - rev_growth
    valid = (
        fresh
        & (surprise > 0.0)
        & (credit_wedge > 0.0)
        & (cash_growth > 0.0)
        & rev_growth.notna()
    )

    raw = rank(surprise.where(valid)) + rank(credit_wedge.where(valid))
    event_score = rank(raw).where(valid, 0.5).where(fresh)
    return event_score.ffill(limit=6)


@register_factor
class ValidatedTradeCreditDemandResponse(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "validated_trade_credit_demand_response"
    name = "Cash-Validated Trade-Credit Demand"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Ranks fresh positive revenue surprises with receivables growth above "
        "sales growth when operating cash flow is also growing, identifying "
        "cash-validated commercial credit expansion."
    )
    window_length = 1
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "revenueGrowth",
        "receivablesGrowth",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        signal = _validated_credit_demand(
            data["revenueGrowth"],
            data["receivablesGrowth"],
            data["revenueSurprise"],
            data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"],
        )
        return signal.reindex(index=template.index, columns=template.columns).fillna(0.5)

Investors often initially discount the revenue beat because they focus on receivables and deteriorating collection optics, while the cash-flow confirmation makes outright revenue-recognition failure less likely; subsequent recognition of the demand signal should support returns over the next six bars. This is falsifiable: the positive return spread should be concentrated in positive-surprise firms with both excess receivables growth and positive operating-cash-flow growth, and should vanish or reverse when cash flow does not validate the expansion.

"""Unaccepted repair adverse selection: repaired selloffs that remain unaccepted predict drift lower.

Mechanism: a high-volume downside excursion can be repaired intraday by temporary
liquidity provision rather than by fundamental demand.  When that repair still
fails to recover the prior close, the closing price reveals incomplete acceptance
of the rebound and likely persistent adverse sell pressure over the next week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _neutral_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank, with ineligible observations kept neutral."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return clean.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class UnacceptedRepairAdverseSelection(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "unaccepted_repair_adverse_selection_h6"
    name = "Unaccepted Repair Adverse Selection"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Abnormal-volume downside excursions substantially repaired from their "
        "lows but still closing below the prior close; high scores indicate "
        "temporary absorption and subsequent adverse-selection drift."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        low = data["low"].where(data["low"] > 0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].where(data["volume"] > 0.0)
        previous_close = close.shift(1)

        # Measure the sell excursion against a strictly pre-event downside norm.
        downside = ((previous_close - low) / previous_close).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.35)
        downside_base = downside.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=30).median()
        downside_surprise = (
            downside / downside_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)

        # Current participation is compared only with prior trading activity.
        volume_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        relative_volume = (volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=12.0)
        activity = np.log1p(relative_volume)

        # Repair is meaningful only relative to the excursion from the prior close.
        excursion = (previous_close - low).where(previous_close > low)
        repair_fraction = ((close - low) / excursion).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        # The key distinction from a completed forced sale: the rebound did not
        # regain the prior closing level, so the market did not accept the repair.
        unaccepted = close < previous_close
        score = (downside_surprise * activity * repair_fraction).where(unaccepted)

        return _neutral_rank(score).reindex(
            index=data["close"].index,
            columns=data["close"].columns,
        )

programs.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized sign implies that a high-volume downside wick repaired before the close is often not forced-sale completion: when the close still fails to regain the prior close, the repair is more plausibly temporary liquidity provision against informed or persistent sell pressure. This child therefore identifies an unaccepted rebound rather than a completed liquidation, predicting delayed downside as sellers continue distributing into the apparent resilience. The edge can persist because daily-bar participants cannot directly observe intraday order-flow ownership or distinguish genuine demand from market-maker inventory absorption; it is falsified if its negative six-bar IC vanishes after controlling for daily return, downside range, relative volume, and sector return.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank

    category = "other"

    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",

        "investedCapital",
        "roic",
        "workingCapital",
        "totalAssets",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        capital = data["investedCapital"].where(data["investedCapital"] > 0.0)
        assets = data["totalAssets"].where(data["totalAssets"] > 0.0)

        cash_return = (data["operatingCashFlow"] / capital).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        roic = data["roic"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_excess = rank(cash_return) - rank(roic)

        prior_assets = assets.shift(63)
        working_capital_change = (
            (data["workingCapital"] - data["workingCapital"].shift(63))
            / prior_assets
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        harvest = (-working_capital_change).clip(lower=0.0)

        fragility = cash_excess * rank(harvest)
        sector_relative = indneutralize(fragility, data["sector"])
        return rank(sector_relative).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A high operating-cash-return residual is not necessarily evidence of superior cash profitability: when it coincides with a sharp decline in working capital, it can reflect inventory liquidation, receivable collection, or delayed payments rather than durable operating improvement. Investors often initially reward the cash-flow headline, but the unsustainable source of the cash is reassessed as operating capital and future conversion normalize, producing negative six-bar returns for the highest signal names. This is falsified if the sector-neutral cash-return residual combined with working-capital release does not predict lower forward returns, especially after controlling for reported ROIC. The edge can persist because headline cash-flow screens rarely distinguish recurring cash generation from temporary balance-sheet release, while trading the correction requires forensic interpretation of quarterly statements.

High values identify apparently cash-productive firms whose cash flow is most plausibly supported by temporary working-capital harvesting.

"""Ownership-anchored earnings reaction-deficit drift.

Mechanism: a signed earnings surprise has remaining information when its
same-day idiosyncratic price reaction is too small in the same direction.
The reaction deficit is more credible when reported per-share economics are
not diluted, allowing filing-level ownership information to be assimilated
gradually after the headline response.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_flag(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally identify the first bar of each available step-function update."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    return clean.notna() & (prior.isna() | clean.ne(prior))


def _event_carry(value: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame, carry: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Freeze an event-date measurement for a finite, causal holding clock."""
    return value.where(event).ffill(limit=carry - 1)


@register_factor
class OwnershipAnchoredReactionDeficitDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "ownership_anchored_reaction_deficit_drift"
    name = "Ownership-Anchored Reaction Deficit Drift"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Fresh EPS surprises whose signed idiosyncratic price response is too "
        "small are carried for six bars, with greater weight for stable or "
        "declining reported share count."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ["close", "epsSurprise", "sharesGrowth"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        share_growth = data["sharesGrowth"].reindex_like(close)

        event = _update_flag(surprise)

        # Remove the common daily tape move before ranking the event response.
        ret = close.pct_change()
        market_move = ret.median(axis=1)
        idio_response = ret.sub(market_move, axis=0)

        # Ranks are taken on the event date and then frozen: later price moves
        # cannot redefine whether the original disclosure was underreacted to.
        surprise_rank = rank(surprise) - 0.5
        response_rank = rank(idio_response) - 0.5
        ownership_credibility = rank(-share_growth)

        event_surprise = _event_carry(surprise_rank, event, 6)
        event_response = _event_carry(response_rank, event, 6)
        event_credibility = _event_carry(ownership_credibility, event, 6)

        deficit = event_surprise - event_response
        aligned_underreaction = (event_surprise * deficit) > 0.0
        active = event_surprise.notna() & event_response.notna() & event_credibility.notna()

        # Positive surprise plus muted upside gives a positive score; negative
        # surprise plus muted downside gives a negative score.
        score = (event_surprise * deficit.abs() * event_credibility).where(
            active & aligned_underreaction
        )
        return rank(score).where(active & aligned_underreaction).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Ownership-Anchored Reaction Deficit Drift
programs.trading_idea: An earnings surprise should continue to drift when the initial price response understates its signed information content, but only when existing shareholders retain a credible claim on the reported earnings through stable or declining share count. This is a delayed-assimilation mechanism: the market processes the headline immediately, while investors more slowly reconcile the surprise with the filing's ownership economics and the unusually muted initial reaction. The edge should persist over six daily bars because institutional investors and fundamental analysts need time to validate whether a muted reaction reflects temporary attention scarcity rather than weak per-share economics; it is falsifiable because positive surprises with both low dilution and reaction deficits should outperform similarly credible surprises that were fully priced on the event day.
programs.description: On fresh EPS-surprise updates, the signal freezes the surprise's cross-sectional rank, its same-day idiosyncratic price-response rank, and share-count credibility for six bars. It is long positive surprises whose initial idiosyncratic reaction is too weak and short negative surprises whose downside reaction is too weak, with greater weight for lower share growth.

"""Receivable-forensics fade after superficially strong revenue reports.

Mechanism: a revenue beat accompanied by receivables outpacing sales is adverse
when it also coincides with slower collection and weaker cash conversion.  Such
reports can initially attract headline-driven buying, but detailed reconciliation
of accrual earnings and customer credit exposure is incorporated more gradually.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _forensic_beat_score(
    revenue_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    receivables_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    days_sales_outstanding: pd.DataFrame,
    income_quality: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Create a causal, report-date score for uncollected revenue beats.

    Fundamental series are point-in-time quarterly step functions.  A change in
    revenue surprise identifies a newly available report.  The 63-bar changes
    compare the current report with the preceding quarterly observation using
    only information available at the current date.
    """
    rev_g = revenue_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    rec_g = receivables_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    surprise = revenue_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    dso = days_sales_outstanding.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    quality = income_quality.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    fresh = surprise.notna() & surprise.ne(surprise.shift(1))
    credit_wedge = rec_g - rev_g
    dso_change = dso - dso.shift(63)
    quality_change = quality - quality.shift(63)

    valid = (
        fresh
        & (surprise > 0.0)
        & credit_wedge.notna()
        & dso_change.notna()
        & quality_change.notna()
    )

    # High wedge, rising DSO, and falling cash conversion jointly indicate that
    # the headline sales beat is least likely to be cash-realized.
    credit_rank = rank(credit_wedge.where(valid))
    dso_rank = rank(dso_change.where(valid))
    weak_cash_rank = 1.0 - rank(quality_change.where(valid))
    score = ((credit_rank + dso_rank + weak_cash_rank) / 3.0).where(valid)

    # The forecast horizon begins at report availability; do not let a stale
    # quarterly observation masquerade as a persistent daily signal.
    return score.ffill(limit=6).fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class ReceivableForensicsCashqualityBeatFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "receivable_forensics_cashquality_beat_fade"
    name = "Receivable Forensics Beat Fade"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Fresh positive revenue beats ranked by receivables growth beyond sales, "
        "DSO deterioration, and weakening income quality; high scores flag "
        "cash-unrealized sales likely to fade."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "revenueGrowth",
        "receivablesGrowth",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "daysSalesOutstanding",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        signal = _forensic_beat_score(
            data["revenueGrowth"],
            data["receivablesGrowth"],
            data["revenueSurprise"],
            data["daysSalesOutstanding"],
            data["incomeQuality"],
        )
        return signal.reindex(index=template.index, columns=template.columns).fillna(0.5)

programs.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC suggests that a positive revenue surprise combined with unusually rapid receivables growth is more often interpreted correctly as a credit-quality warning than as productive customer onboarding. The child distinguishes this adverse selection channel from healthy contractual ramping by requiring contemporaneous deterioration in cash-conversion quality: rising days-sales-outstanding and falling operating-cash-flow-to-net-income quality. The edge should persist for several days because investors initially anchor on the headline beat, while reconciling collections, accruals, and working-capital disclosures requires slower fundamental attention; it is falsified if these jointly adverse reports do not underperform other positive-surprise reports over the next six bars.

Higher values identify beats whose reported sales appear least cash-realized and are expected to precede lower returns.

"""Peer-backlog silent cash delivery.

Mechanism: a sequence of peer filings creates an analyst attention queue.  Cash-confirmed
multi-line issuer updates with neither an unusual idiosyncratic move nor unusual
volume are likely to be processed only after that queue clears.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _signed_change(frame: pd.DataFrame, direction: float) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Point-in-time report-to-report signed change and update indicator."""
    prior = frame.shift(1)
    valid = frame.notna() & prior.notna()
    change = frame - prior
    signed = np.sign(direction * change).where(valid, np.nan)
    updated = change.ne(0.0) & valid
    return signed, updated


def _industry_mean(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional industry mean at each date."""
    return frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T


@register_factor
class PeerBacklogSilentCashDelivery(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_backlog_silent_cash_delivery"
    name = "Peer Backlog Silent Cash Delivery"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Cash-confirmed broad operating updates weighted by a leave-one-out "
        "industry filing backlog and filtered for low contemporaneous price "
        "and volume attention."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "revenue",
        "grossMargin",
        "operatingMargin",
        "roic",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "debtToEquity",
        "revenuePerShare",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        revenue = data["revenue"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ocf_margin = data["operatingCashFlow"] / revenue
        fcf_margin = data["freeCashFlow"] / revenue

        fields = (
            (data["grossMargin"], 1.0),
            (data["operatingMargin"], 1.0),
            (data["roic"], 1.0),
            (ocf_margin, 1.0),
            (fcf_margin, 1.0),
            (data["debtToEquity"], -1.0),
            (data["revenuePerShare"], 1.0),
        )

        signed_parts: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        update_parts: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        for frame, direction in fields:
            signed, updated = _signed_change(frame, direction)
            signed_parts.append(signed)
            update_parts.append(updated)

        signed_panel = pd.concat(signed_parts, keys=range(len(signed_parts)))
        update_panel = pd.concat(update_parts, keys=range(len(update_parts)))
        breadth = signed_panel.groupby(level=1).mean()
        update_count = update_panel.groupby(level=1).sum()

        material = update_count.ge(5.0)
        cash_agrees = (
            signed_parts[3].notna()
            & signed_parts[4].notna()
            & signed_parts[3].mul(breadth).gt(0.0)
            & signed_parts[4].mul(breadth).gt(0.0)
        )
        event = (material & cash_agrees).astype(float)
        signed_event = breadth.mul(update_count / float(len(fields))).where(
            material & cash_agrees,
            0.0,
        ).fillna(0.0)

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns).fillna("Unknown")
        industry_activity = _industry_mean(event, labels).fillna(0.0)
        group_size = labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("size").astype(float)
        peer_activity = (
            industry_activity.mul(group_size, axis=1).sub(event)
            .div(group_size.sub(1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=1)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
        peer_backlog = peer_activity.ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        industry_return = _industry_mean(daily_return, labels)
        idio_return = daily_return - industry_return
        prior_idio_vol = idio_return.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().shift(1)
        reaction_ratio = idio_return.abs() / prior_idio_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        prior_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().shift(1)
        volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        excess_volume_attention = np.log(volume_ratio).clip(lower=0.0)
        total_attention = reaction_ratio.clip(lower=0.0) + excess_volume_attention
        silent_weight = (1.0 / (1.0 + total_attention)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        silent_weight = silent_weight.where(prior_volume.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        raw_signal = signed_event * peer_backlog * silent_weight
        signal = rank(raw_signal) - 0.5
        return signal.reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Peer Backlog Silent Cash Delivery
programs.trading_idea: Industry reporting congestion should create a multi-day attention queue rather than merely a same-day distraction: analysts must process several comparable filings, allocate follow-up work, and update relative models sequentially. The child therefore selects cash-confirmed broad operating updates that occur while peer report activity has accumulated over recent days, but whose own price and volume response indicate that the issuer has not yet received immediate market attention. The edge should persist because processing cross-firm cash-flow, margin, and capital-efficiency implications is costly and cannot be fully arbitraged from a single headline; it is falsified if silent updates in high peer-backlog states do not outperform equivalent silent updates with little accumulated peer activity over the next six bars.
programs.description: Ranks signed, cash-confirmed multi-line fundamental updates by a leave-one-out exponentially decayed industry report backlog, while downweighting updates already accompanied by unusual idiosyncratic returns or volume. Positive broad improvements receive positive scores and broad deteriorations receive negative scores.

"""Congested cash delivery adverse-auction repair.

Mechanism: when a broad cash-confirmed operating update is released amid peer
filing congestion, an abnormal opening auction in the opposite direction is
more likely to be temporary liquidity pressure than an informed repricing.
Financial resilience increases the credibility of positive delivery, while
fragility increases the credibility of negative delivery.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _signed_change(frame: pd.DataFrame, direction: float) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal report-to-report signed change and a valid update indicator."""
    prior = frame.shift(1)
    valid = frame.notna() & prior.notna()
    change = frame - prior
    signed = np.sign(direction * change).where(valid, np.nan)
    updated = change.ne(0.0) & valid
    return signed, updated


def _industry_mean(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-date industry mean, retaining the original ticker layout."""
    return frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T


def _auction_impulse(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Signed, volume-confirmed opening-auction continuation impulse."""
    prior_close = close.shift(1)
    prior_range = (high.shift(1) - low.shift(1)).abs()
    fallback = prior_close.abs() * 0.01
    scale = prior_range.where(prior_range > 0.0, fallback).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    gap = (open_ - prior_close) / scale
    gap_sign = np.sign(gap)
    gap_size = gap.abs()
    retention = gap_sign * (close - open_) / (gap_size * scale).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    retention = retention.clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)

    day_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = (2.0 * close - high - low) / day_range
    directional_location = gap_sign * close_location

    normal_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=12).median()
    rel_volume = volume / normal_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    volume_weight = np.log1p(rel_volume.clip(lower=0.0)).clip(upper=np.log(8.0))
    confirmation = (0.65 * retention + 0.35 * directional_location).clip(-2.0, 2.0)

    impulse = gap_sign * np.tanh(gap_size / 2.0) * confirmation * volume_weight
    return impulse.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _resilience(
    roic: pd.DataFrame,
    fcf_yield: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_assets: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional PIT capacity score used only to validate event polarity."""
    return (
        rank(roic).fillna(0.5)
        + rank(fcf_yield).fillna(0.5)
        + rank(-debt_to_assets).fillna(0.5)
    ) / 3.0


@register_factor
class CongestedCashDeliveryAdverseAuctionRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "congested_cash_delivery_adverse_auction_repair"
    name = "Congested Cash Delivery Adverse Auction Repair"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Trades against a sector-relative abnormal-volume opening auction when it "
        "contradicts a cash-confirmed operating update released into peer filing congestion."
    )
    window_length = 31
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "revenue",
        "grossMargin",
        "operatingMargin",
        "roic",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "debtToEquity",
        "revenuePerShare",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "debtToAssets",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        revenue = data["revenue"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ocf_margin = data["operatingCashFlow"] / revenue
        fcf_margin = data["freeCashFlow"] / revenue

        fields = (
            (data["grossMargin"], 1.0),
            (data["operatingMargin"], 1.0),
            (data["roic"], 1.0),
            (ocf_margin, 1.0),
            (fcf_margin, 1.0),
            (data["debtToEquity"], -1.0),
            (data["revenuePerShare"], 1.0),
        )
        signed_parts = []
        update_parts = []
        for frame, direction in fields:
            signed, updated = _signed_change(frame, direction)
            signed_parts.append(signed)
            update_parts.append(updated)

        signed_panel = pd.concat(signed_parts, keys=range(len(signed_parts)))
        update_panel = pd.concat(update_parts, keys=range(len(update_parts)))
        breadth = signed_panel.groupby(level=1).mean()
        update_count = update_panel.groupby(level=1).sum()

        material = update_count.ge(5.0)
        cash_agrees = (
            signed_parts[3].notna()
            & signed_parts[4].notna()
            & signed_parts[3].mul(breadth).gt(0.0)
            & signed_parts[4].mul(breadth).gt(0.0)
        )
        valid_event = material & cash_agrees
        signed_event = (breadth * update_count / float(len(fields))).where(valid_event, 0.0)
        event = valid_event.astype(float)

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns).fillna("Unknown")
        industry_activity = _industry_mean(event, labels).fillna(0.0)
        group_size = labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("size").astype(float)
        peer_activity = (
            industry_activity.mul(group_size, axis=1)
            .sub(event)
            .div(group_size.sub(1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=1)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
        peer_backlog = peer_activity.ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        industry_return = _industry_mean(daily_return, labels)
        idio_return = daily_return - industry_return
        prior_idio_vol = idio_return.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().shift(1)
        favorable_reaction = (
            signed_event * idio_return / prior_idio_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0)
        unpriced_weight = (1.0 / (1.0 + favorable_reaction)).fillna(0.0)

        auction = _auction_impulse(
            data["open"], data["high"], data["low"], close, volume
        )
        sector_auction = indneutralize(auction, data["sector"].fillna("Unknown"))
        contradiction = (-sector_auction * signed_event).gt(0.0)

        resilience = _resilience(
            data["roic"], data["freeCashFlowYield"], data["debtToAssets"]
        )
        polarity_capacity = resilience.where(signed_event >= 0.0, 1.0 - resilience)
        raw_signal = (
            -sector_auction
            * signed_event.abs()
            * peer_backlog
            * polarity_capacity
            * unpriced_weight
        ).where(contradiction, 0.0)

        signal = rank(raw_signal.fillna(0.0)) - 0.5
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A cash-confirmed, broad operating improvement arriving during an industry filing backlog is vulnerable to delayed analyst processing, especially when the market has not already moved in the update's direction. If that issuer simultaneously experiences a volume-confirmed opening-auction move opposite to the update, the tape is more likely to reflect temporary inventory pressure or attention displacement than informed disagreement; resilient firms have greater capacity for this repair. Neither parent alone identifies this contradiction: peer congestion identifies delayed fundamental assimilation but not an actively adverse liquidity shock, while the auction fade cannot distinguish a generic dislocation from one directly contradicted by unprocessed cash delivery.
programs.description: The signal detects broad cash-confirmed report-to-report operating updates, weights them by leave-one-out industry filing backlog and balance-sheet capacity, and takes the opposite side of a sector-relative abnormal-volume auction impulse when the auction contradicts the update.

"""Conflicted-congestion relative cash relay.

Mechanism: a cash-confirmed issuer update is slow to enter relative valuations when
many industry peers report simultaneously but provide conflicting directional evidence.
The signal selects issuer-specific outliers with little immediate tape recognition.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _signed_change(frame: pd.DataFrame, direction: float) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal report-to-report directional change and update mask."""
    prior = frame.shift(1)
    valid = frame.notna() & prior.notna()
    change = frame - prior
    signed = np.sign(direction * change).where(valid, np.nan)
    updated = change.ne(0.0) & valid
    return signed, updated


def _industry_mean(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T


def _leave_one_out(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out same-date peer mean, zero for singleton industries."""
    mean = _industry_mean(frame, labels)
    size = labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("size").astype(float)
    numerator = mean.mul(size, axis=1).sub(frame)
    denominator = size.sub(1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return numerator.div(denominator, axis=1).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class ConflictedCongestionRelativeCashRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "conflicted_congestion_relative_cash_relay"
    name = "Conflicted Congestion Relative Cash Relay"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Signed cash-confirmed fundamental outliers versus leave-one-out industry "
        "peers, activated only during dense and directionally conflicted peer reporting "
        "with a muted immediate idiosyncratic tape response."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "revenue",
        "grossMargin",
        "operatingMargin",
        "roic",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "debtToEquity",
        "revenuePerShare",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        revenue = data["revenue"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ocf_margin = data["operatingCashFlow"].div(revenue)
        fcf_margin = data["freeCashFlow"].div(revenue)

        fields = (
            (data["grossMargin"], 1.0),
            (data["operatingMargin"], 1.0),
            (data["roic"], 1.0),
            (ocf_margin, 1.0),
            (fcf_margin, 1.0),
            (data["debtToEquity"], -1.0),
            (data["revenuePerShare"], 1.0),
        )

        signs: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        updates: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        for frame, direction in fields:
            signed, updated = _signed_change(frame, direction)
            signs.append(signed)
            updates.append(updated)

        sign_panel = pd.concat(signs, keys=range(len(signs)))
        update_panel = pd.concat(updates, keys=range(len(updates)))
        breadth = sign_panel.groupby(level=1).mean()
        update_count = update_panel.groupby(level=1).sum()

        material = update_count.ge(5.0)
        cash_confirmed = (
            signs[3].notna()
            & signs[4].notna()
            & signs[3].mul(breadth).gt(0.0)
            & signs[4].mul(breadth).gt(0.0)
        )
        active = material & cash_confirmed
        delivery = breadth.mul(update_count / float(len(fields))).where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns).fillna("Unknown")
        peer_delivery = _leave_one_out(delivery, labels)
        peer_square = _leave_one_out(delivery.pow(2), labels)
        peer_activity = _leave_one_out(active.astype(float), labels)
        peer_abs_delivery = _leave_one_out(delivery.abs(), labels)

        peer_var = peer_square.sub(peer_delivery.pow(2)).clip(lower=0.0)
        peer_scale = np.sqrt(peer_var).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_outlier = delivery.sub(peer_delivery).div(peer_scale).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        group_size = labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("size").astype(float)
        peer_share = (1.0 - 1.0 / group_size).clip(lower=0.0)
        congestion = peer_activity.mul(peer_share, axis=1)
        disagreement = peer_abs_delivery.sub(peer_delivery.abs()).clip(lower=0.0)
        conflict_gate = disagreement.div(peer_abs_delivery.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)

        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        industry_return = _industry_mean(daily_return, labels)
        idio_return = daily_return.sub(industry_return)
        prior_volatility = idio_return.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().shift(1)
        price_attention = idio_return.abs().div(prior_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        prior_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().shift(1)
        volume_attention = np.log(volume.div(prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))).clip(lower=0.0)
        attention = price_attention.clip(lower=0.0).add(volume_attention, fill_value=0.0)
        quiet_weight = (1.0 / (1.0 + attention)).where(prior_volume.notna(), 0.0)
        quiet_weight = quiet_weight.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        raw = relative_outlier.mul(congestion).mul(conflict_gate).mul(quiet_weight).where(active)
        signal = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(active, 0.0)
        return signal.reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Conflicted Congestion Relative Cash Relay
programs.trading_idea: The child isolates cash-confirmed, broad issuer updates that are directionally exceptional versus their own industry peers, but only when the peer reporting calendar is both crowded and internally conflicted. Congestion alone creates limited attention, while peer disagreement specifically prevents analysts from quickly mapping an issuer's result into relative-value models; the issuer-level outlier is therefore delayed rather than merely unnoticed. A muted contemporaneous idiosyncratic price-and-volume response identifies the cases where this unresolved comparative-information burden remains available to diffuse over the fixed six-day horizon.
programs.description: Ranks signed, cash-confirmed multi-line fundamental deliveries by their leave-one-out industry outlier score, gated by simultaneous peer reporting density and peer directional disagreement, then downweights immediately noticed events. Positive exceptional deliveries are long and negative exceptional deliveries are short.
